title: Vitals grid shows a clipped sliver beside the names: on desktop when it opens, on a phone after a swipe to the end
evidence: Done 2026-11-14: styles.css rounds the vitals grid's scroll range up to whole date columns (width: calc(100% + round(up, natural - 100%, --bt-value-w)); the filler before Trend takes the rest) and snaps it (scroll-snap-type: x mandatory, scroll-padding-left = the name column, scroll-snap-align: start on the header date columns, New and the filler). So the right edge, where the table opens, is a whole column on a phone and a desktop, New stays clear of a sticky Trend, and a swipe settles on a whole column, its end included. useValuePage.ts drops H79's sticky-Trend case: it opens every grid at its right edge, and the vitals grid with New whole beside the names where the range ends past New (320). A focusin handler moves a cut vitals cell beside the names: WebKit centres a focused input and the snap rounded that to the nearer column, cutting the BP cell 15 px at 375. Real WebKit and Chromium, 13 weights: 390 opens 1183/1183, 1440 opens 738/738 (New 60 px clear of Trend), 320 opens 1183/1274 and swipes to 1274 for Trend; no clipped column after open, 1 s later, a swipe or any focus. Was: From D2 (the phone fade after H79; first written as H102 on PR 1712, which was dropped; H102 is now PR 1714's). Desktop: at 1440 in real WebKit, with 13 saved weights, the vitals grid opens at scrollLeft 678 of 678: Trend is sticky at the right (styles.css .bt-timeline-scroll .bt-cell-trend), New 818-900, Trend 900-954. The left-most visible date column sits partly under the sticky name column, so only its "ys / dia" tail shows. H79 snaps whole columns only where Trend scrolls (widget-src/src/lib/useValuePage.ts:85-95). Phone: at 390, after a swipe to the end, a "lia" sliver (the tail of an older column's "sys / dia") shows beside the name column. H79's snap runs only when the grid is shown; a swipe ends at max scrollLeft (scrollWidth - clientWidth), which is not a whole column. Shot: d2-fade-390-end.png in session 701729d1's scratchpad. Remedy: on desktop, snap the left edge to a whole column with the sticky Trend's width taken out of max, so New stays clear of Trend; on a phone, make the scroll end on a whole column too. (H105)
